page: OVHcloud b2-15 is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Haswell processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, resulting in 4 vCPUs. It is equipped with 15.0 GB of RAM, yielding 3.75 GB of memory per core, and includes 100 GB of local SSD storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the underlying Intel Haswell hardware delivers modest processing capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance and PassMark CPU scores are positioned in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed; cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 347.69 GB/sec, but large-block read and write bandwidths drop to the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations and small-model LLM inference achieve average tier results, whereas larger workloads like 7B LLM inference and Redis SET operations perform in the lower percentiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the b2-15 offers dedicated CPU resources and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio without the premium of high-performance modern architectures. This makes it a viable option for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high-frequency processing or advanced instruction sets like AVX-512. Suitable workloads include basic web serving, lightweight database operations, small-scale message queuing, and development or testing environments.
